name: New York Control to Invisible Collar
summary: The move to Invisible Collar adds a high second-leg closure after arm isolation and neck clearing, reinforcing the bottom player's rubber-guard posture control.
description: New York Control to Invisible Collar isolates an arm and clears the neck before adding the second leg high behind the head to reinforce posture control.
overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York Control, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Clear the neck through the Chill Dog checkpoint before adding the second leg. Neither a jacket collar nor rear hooks define this route.

Keep the elbow separated from an inside frame before closing the second leg. Maintain the cleared hand position and knee hug as the free leg comes higher. Bring the second leg into the high clinch through hip motion; do not pull the foot into position against resistance.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (bottom): Where must their isolated elbow stay?
flashcards.answer: Keep the opponent's arm isolated outside before the second leg closes; an elbow recovered inside can rebuild their frame.

plausible: Back between your chests as a frame
Between your high thigh and chest as an inside wedge
trap: Outside your hand grip but inside the knee hug

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (bottom): What stays connected as the free leg rises?
flashcards.answer: The reinforcing leg is added to an existing neck-cleared arm trap without abandoning the supporting knee hug.
flashcards.answer_line: The overhook, knee hug and cleared head-side arm

plausible: Only the hand pulling the back of the head
Only a foot on the opponent's hip
trap: The knee hug alone after the head-side grip is released

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (bottom): How should the second leg reach its high closure?
flashcards.answer: Use hip mobility to bring the reinforcing leg high behind the head instead of hauling the foot against a fixed knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Through hip movement behind the opponent's head

plausible: By crossing the ankles low behind their waist
With the second knee below the opponent's shoulder
trap: By pulling the foot up while the knee stays pinned

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (bottom): What retains this isolated-arm posture clinch?
flashcards.answer: Invisible Collar reinforces the existing leg-and-arm clinch; keeping the whole connection close matters more than isolated head traction.
flashcards.answer_line: The connected high legs and arm trap

plausible: A single loose foot behind an upright head
Two high feet with the isolated elbow framing inside
trap: A tight head grip with the second leg still below the shoulder

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (bottom): Their elbow slips inside; what should you recognize?
flashcards.answer: A recovered inside elbow can undermine the original trap even if both legs remain high; assess the arm relationship before continuing.

plausible: The second leg must now be the only control that matters
The trapped wrist still proves that New York is intact
trap: The inside elbow is merely slack within an unchanged arm trap

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (bottom): Knee discomfort under a stack: what next?
flashcards.answer: Release the high connection and return to a comfortable guard when stacking or knee discomfort makes it unsustainable.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the high clinch and recover inside frames

plausible: Keep both legs high and pull the feet closer
Let the knee drift while tightening the head grip
trap: Keep the high-leg grip while lowering only the free foot

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (bottom): What precedes adding the second leg?
flashcards.answer: New York supplies posture control and an isolated arm; then clear the head-side arm before reinforcing the high clinch.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing guard with posture down and one arm isolated

plausible: Facing guard with both elbows braced inside
Facing guard with posture upright and one wrist held
trap: Facing guard with posture low but both elbows inside

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (bottom): What precedes the second-leg closure?
flashcards.answer: Clear the head-side arm through the Chill Dog checkpoint while preserving the overhook and knee hug before adding the second leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Neck clearing with the knee hug retained

plausible: Returning the trapped hand to the opponent's chest
Closing both high legs before the head-side arm clears
trap: Releasing the knee hug to make room for the free leg

defender.name: New York Control to Invisible Collar Defender
defender.description: New York Control to Invisible Collar (defender): The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure.
defender.overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York Control, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Clear the neck through the Chill Dog checkpoint before adding the second leg. Neither a jacket collar nor rear hooks define this route.

The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure. Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.

Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm. Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens. Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.
key_principles: Recognize the high closure: The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip.
Protect the neck and arm: Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure.
Keep a balanced base: Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.
Address the leg enclosure: Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm.
Recover inside position: Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens.
Stop on compression: Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (top): Which cue marks the extra reinforcement?
flashcards.answer: The second leg closing high reinforces the existing arm-and-leg clinch, so recognize it before it completes.
flashcards.answer_line: Their free leg climbing behind your head

plausible: Their high leg lowering off your shoulder
Their near knee returning below your chest
trap: Their controlling hand regrips the same high ankle

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (top): How should the caught shoulder stay aligned?
flashcards.answer: Keep the captured elbow compact and avoid rotating your torso away from a fixed shoulder while seeking slack.
flashcards.answer_line: Head and torso aligned, elbow near the ribs

plausible: Head away while the elbow remains pinned
Elbow wide while the chest turns back
trap: Head upright while the elbow remains outside the knee hug

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (top): Which response addresses the high closure early?
flashcards.answer: Early inside space and a balanced base can deny the reinforcing leg before it closes; do not rely on late forced extraction.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame inside before the second leg connects

plausible: Wait until both legs close before seeking space
Reach both hands behind the opponent's back
trap: Post both hands outside their hips as the leg climbs

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (top): What should open before you raise your head?
flashcards.answer: Create slack in the high enclosure before recovering head height so the movement does not pull against a fixed loop.
flashcards.answer_line: The high-leg connection at the hip and thigh

plausible: Only your knee spacing on the mat
Only your free hand while the head stays cinched
trap: Only the second ankle while the first high leg stays tight

flashcards.question: New York Control to Invisible Collar (top): Where should the arm return as the loop opens?
flashcards.answer: When the shoulder can move, return the elbow between the bodies to prevent renewed outside-arm isolation.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside beside the ribs, available to frame

plausible: Outside on the mat with the elbow flared
Across the partner's far shoulder
trap: Hand on the sternum with the elbow left beyond their knee
